clue.text: Fruit, overly dull inside

indicators.note: inside says the second word sits within the letters of the first

parts.note: overly means too much, as in 'too keen'
matt or mat describes a dull, unglossy finish

explanation.surface: A complaint about some fruit whose inside is boringly flavourless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dull' reads as a flavour verdict on the fruit, but it means matt, a finish without shine.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically the tomato is a berry, so it counts as a fruit even if cooks treat it as a vegetable.

clue.text: Couple raising swine in volume

indicators.note: in places the turned animal inside the book word

parts.note: a tome is a large book or volume

indicators.note: in a down clue raising lifts the word up, so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: a sow is a female pig

explanation.surface: A farming couple rearing pigs, written up in a big book.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the reversal reads upward, which is why 'raising' works here.
explanation.definitionFit: A twosome is a pair of people together, so it means a couple.

clue.text: Sportsmen in the end returning from underworld

indicators.note: returning means the combination is read back the other way
in places the sports body inside the word for end

parts.note: an aim is an end, a goal
FA is the Football Association

explanation.surface: Athletes finally coming back from the land of the dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the end' looks like 'finally'; here 'the end' is a noun meaning a goal, with the sportsmen placed in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The underworld is organised crime, and the Mafia is its most famous syndicate.

clue.text: Blunt, say, or characteristic in front

indicators.note: in front says the characteristic is placed before the little word

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bluntness is described as a characteristic that shows on the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blunt' looks like an adjective; it is Anthony Blunt, the art historian exposed as a Soviet spy.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Blunt betrayed Britain by spying for the Soviet Union, an example of a traitor.

clue.text: Fabulist losing way and breaking bone

indicators.note: something breaking falls apart, so what remains is rearranged
losing tells us some letters are dropped from the long word before it

parts.note: taken as written: a teller of fables
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: A teller of tall tales loses their way and breaks a bone, like a cautionary fable.
explanation.walkthrough: Take ST out of FABULIST to leave FABULI, then rearrange it.
explanation.definitionFit: The fibula is the slender outer bone of the human lower leg, running beside the shin.

clue.text: It's wrong to get trimmer middle by using mouth

indicators.note: middle keeps only the central letters of the word before it

parts.note: the middle three of seven letters
oral means of the mouth

explanation.surface: A dieting warning: it is wrong to slim your waist by eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Immoral means morally wrong, against accepted standards of right conduct.

clue.text: See into dissolved whole

indicators.note: into puts the Latin look word inside the word for dissolved

parts.note: undid means dissolved or annulled
vide is Latin for see, used in references

explanation.surface: An instruction to look into something dissolved as a whole.
explanation.walkthrough: Vide, Latin for 'see', survives in English footnotes as a cross-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: Undivided means not split into parts, complete and entire.

clue.text: Tanks, as in song

indicators.note: in places the Latin-derived word inside the word for song

parts.note: an aria is an operatic song
qua means as, in the capacity of

explanation.surface: Tanks treated as if they were part of an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Qua is a Latin word used in English to mean 'in the role of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquaria are glass tanks for keeping fish, the plural of aquarium.

clue.text: Eliot and Milne, flanking Wells, recoil in horror

indicators.note: to recoil is to spring back, so the whole string reads backwards

parts.note: T. S. Eliot, the poet

indicators.note: flanking means standing on either side, so the pair of initials go round the other

parts.note: A. A. Milne, author of Winnie-the-Pooh
H. G. Wells, the novelist

explanation.surface: Three English writers shrink back in horror.
explanation.walkthrough: Each author gives initials: A.A. splits around H.G. to make AHGA after TS; TSAHGA read backwards is AGHAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast means filled with shock and horror, so to be aghast is to be in horror.

clue.text: Wunderkind's hunting pack, crafted in Antipodes, gets market outside them

parts.note: a pack of hunting wolves is a wolf gang

indicators.note: in places the word for crafted within the abbreviation for the southern land

parts.note: AUS is the abbreviation for Australia, the Antipodes
something crafted has been made

indicators.note: outside puts the trading word around the short name the last word stands for

parts.note: a mart is a market
them points back to the Antipodes, Australia, informally Oz

explanation.surface: A child prodigy's pack of hunting dogs, made in Australia, is taken to market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Them' has no letters of its own in the clue: it points back to the Antipodes, whose nickname supplies the middle of the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The composer was the classic child prodigy, touring Europe's courts as a performer at six.

clue.text: See 9
Beast finds far from buxom redhead, God willing, on boat

parts.note: AA is the smallest bra cup size, the opposite of buxom
the head, or first letter, of red
DV stands for Deo volente, Latin for God willing
Noah's boat was the ark

explanation.surface: A beast looks for a flat-chested redhead and, God willing, a boat to sail on.
explanation.walkthrough: Bra cups run from AA (smallest) upward, so AA is far from buxom. DV is the Latin abbreviation of Deo volente.
explanation.definitionFit: The aardvark is an African burrowing mammal that eats ants, so it is a beast or animal.

clue.text: Politician's expletive about comeback

indicators.note: about means the curse wraps round the other piece

parts.note: drat is a mild curse
read as come back: the word come written backwards

explanation.surface: A politician swears on hearing about a rival's comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comeback' looks like a noun for a return; split it as an instruction, come + back.
explanation.definitionFit: A Democrat is a member of the US Democratic Party, a politician in American party terms.

clue.text: Medic's expletive about bard''s comeback

indicators.note: about means the swear word wraps round the other piece

parts.note: an oath is a swear word
a bard is a poet; poet's, written backwards

explanation.surface: A doctor curses about a poet's comeback; a companion to 12 across.
explanation.walkthrough: As in 12 across, 'comeback' is an instruction to read the preceding word backwards, not a return to form.
explanation.definitionFit: An osteopath treats the body by manipulating bones and muscles, a kind of medical practitioner.

clue.text: Classically, Diana features in classical mode

indicators.note: features means includes, so the letters are carried within the words before it

parts.note: found across the end of the first word and most of the second

explanation.surface: In classical myth Diana appears in a classical style.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans classicaLLY DIANa, ignoring the comma.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lydian mode is one of the ancient Greek musical modes, named after Lydia in Asia Minor.

clue.text: Refer to accountant turning acid

indicators.note: turning round means the joined words are read from end to start

parts.note: to cite is to refer to
CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: Someone advises consulting an accountant who is turning sour.
explanation.walkthrough: CITE + CA read backwards gives ACETIC. CA, chartered accountant, is a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetic means of or like vinegar, sharp and sour, and acetic acid is vinegar's active ingredient.

clue.text: Bond embraces leading lady, being good-natured

indicators.note: embraces means holds within, so the bond wraps round the letter

parts.note: cement bonds things together

indicators.note: leading picks out the letter at the front of lady

parts.note: the first letter of lady

explanation.surface: James Bond embraces his leading lady, being nice to her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' looks like 007 with his leading lady; it is the verb or noun for sticking together.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement means mild and merciful in temperament, lenient and kindly.

clue.text: Relative position (originally 10-10) in bed

indicators.note: in places the numbers inside the word for bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: originally means done in an original, inventive way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as the number written in words
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A cryptic note about where something sits, with a scoreline in brackets.
explanation.walkthrough: The two tens are written two different ways, once as a word to be rearranged and once as a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Context is the setting around a word or event, its place in relation to what surrounds it.

clue.text: Card trick involving papers, say

indicators.note: involving means wrapping round, so the trick surrounds the papers

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
newspapers are an example of the media

explanation.surface: A magician's card trick featuring newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Card' looks like a playing card in a trick; here it means a funny person.
explanation.definitionFit: A card is an amusing, eccentric person, a joker, which is what a comedian is.

clue.text: Shout about women producing fruit

indicators.note: about means the shout goes round the word for women

parts.note: a cry is a shout
her stands for a woman

explanation.surface: Someone shouts at women who are selling fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The cherry is a small round stone fruit, red or black, grown on trees.

clue.text: Increasingly bird-like, both curtailed in Central Europe

indicators.note: curtailed means docked at the tail, and both says each of the two words loses its last letter

parts.note: more and more, increasingly
avian means of or like birds

explanation.surface: Something becoming more and more birdlike, both shortened, somewhere in Central Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: MORE loses E and AVIAN loses N.
explanation.definitionFit: Moravia is a historical region of the Czech Republic, which lies in the heart of Central Europe.

clue.text: One is in need of flavouring

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: in puts the little verb inside the word for need

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is in need of some flavouring for the dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads almost literally; 'one' is the letter A and 'is' sits inside 'need'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aniseed is the liquorice-tasting seed of the anise plant, used to flavour sweets and drinks.

clue.text: Repudiate study on weight

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the study comes first and the weight follows

parts.note: a den is a study, a private room
an ounce is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Rejecting a research paper about weight.
explanation.definitionFit: To denounce something is to condemn it publicly, disowning or rejecting it outright.

clue.text: Reply by putting Burn's darling in control

indicators.note: putting the darling in the control word places one inside the other

parts.note: a rein is a means of control
jo is Scots for sweetheart, as in Burns's 'John Anderson, my jo'

explanation.surface: Answering by bringing Robert Burns's beloved under control.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Burns, the Scottish poet, wrote in Scots, where jo means sweetheart, as in 'John Anderson, my jo'.
explanation.definitionFit: To rejoin is to say in answer, a formal word for retort or respond.

clue.text: Drink for a month, almost establishing record

indicators.note: almost says the month name falls one letter short

parts.note: July is a month
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A drinker spends a month nearly setting a record.
explanation.walkthrough: JULY loses its last letter, then EP is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A julep is a sweet iced drink, especially the mint julep of bourbon, sugar and mint.

clue.text: One seeking alternative way to water green valley endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly says the last letter of the word before it is cut off
an alternative way of setting out the letters means rearranging them

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
valley without its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone looking for an alternative route to irrigate a green valley.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition and the anagram signal overlap in spirit: a New Age traveller seeks an alternative way of life.
explanation.definitionFit: New Age travellers are British itinerants who live on the road, seeking a lifestyle apart from mainstream society.

clue.text: Island welcome in French 18 across

indicators.note: in puts the greeting inside the name of the French performer

parts.note: Jacques Tati was a French comic film-maker, and 18 across is COMEDIAN
hi is a word of welcome

explanation.surface: An island greeting delivered in the style of a French comic.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference supplies 'comedian', so a French comedian is Jacques Tati, the film-maker behind Monsieur Hulot.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahiti is the largest island of French Polynesia in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Having played for county, went one better

definitions.meaning: first meaning: awarded a cap for selection to a team
second meaning: outdid or topped someone

explanation.walkthrough: In British sport a player selected for a county or national side is given a cap.
explanation.definitionFit: A capped player has represented a side; to cap a story or achievement is to surpass it.
